Document: Part 61 – Admiralty Claims
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
## Judgment in default

## 61.9

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (1) In an admiralty claim the claimant may obtain judgment in default of –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (a) an acknowledgment of service only if at the date on which judgment is entered–

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (i) the defendant has not filed an acknowledgment of service; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (ii) )the relevant time limit for doing so has expired;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (b) defence only if at the date on which judgment is entered –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (i) a defence has not been filed; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (ii) the relevant time limit for doing so has expired. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (2) In a collision claim, a party who has filed a collision statement of case within the time specified by rule 61.4(5) may obtain judgment in default of a collision statement of case only if at the date on which judgment is entered–

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (a) the party against whom judgment is sought has not filed a collision statement of case; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (b) the time for doing so set out in rule 61.4(5) has expired. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (3) An application for judgment in default –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (a) in a claim in rem must be made by filing –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (i) an application notice as set out in Practice Direction 61;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (ii) a certificate proving service of the claim form; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (iii) evidence proving the claim to the satisfaction of the court; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (b) n a claim in personam must be made in accordance with Part 12 with any necessary modifications. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (4) An application notice seeking judgment in default and, unless the court orders otherwise, all evidence in support, must be served on all persons who have entered cautions against release on the Register. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (5) The court may set aside or vary any judgment in default entered under this rule. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (6) The claimant may apply to the court for judgment against a party at whose instance a notice against arrest was entered where –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (a) the claim form has been served on that party;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (b) the sum claimed in the claim form does not exceed the amount specified in the undertaking given by that party in accordance with rule 61.7(2)(a)(ii); and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.9] (c) that party has not fulfilled that undertaking within 14 days after service on him of the claim form. ## Sale by the court, priorities and payment out

## 61.10

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.10] (1) An application for an order for the survey, appraisement or sale of a ship must set be made in a claim in rem at any stage by any party. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.10] (2) Unless the court is satisfied that there is good reason not to do so, if the court makes an order for sale, it may –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.10] (a)  a time within which notice of claims against the proceeds of sale must be filed; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.10] (b) the time and manner in which that time limit must be advertised. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.10] (3) Any party with a judgment against the property or proceeds of sale may at any time after the time referred to in paragraph (2) apply to the court for the determination of priorities. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.10] (4) An application notice under paragraph (3) must be served on all persons who have filed a claim against the property. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.10] (5) Payment out of the proceeds of sale will be made only to judgment creditors and –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.10] (a) in accordance with the determination of priorities; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.10] (b) as the court orders. ## Limitation claims

## 61.11

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (1) This rule applies to limitation claims. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (2) A claim is started by the issue of a limitation claim form as set out in Practice Direction 61. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (3) The –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) claimant; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) at least one defendant

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] must be named in the claim form, but all other defendants may be described. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (4) The claim form –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) must be served on all named defendants and any other defendant who requests service upon him; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) may be served on any other defendant. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (5) The claim form may not be served out of the jurisdiction unless; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) the claim falls within section 22(2)(a), (b) or (c) of the Supreme Court Act 1981 6 ;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) the defendant has submitted to or agreed to submit to the jurisdiction of the court; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (c) the Admiralty Court has jurisdiction over the claim under any applicable Convention; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] the court grants permission in accordance with Section IV of Part 6. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (d) rule 6.33 applies

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (6) An acknowledgment of service is not required. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (7) Every defendant upon whom a claim form is served must –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) within 28 days of service file –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (i) a defence; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (ii) a notice that the defendant admits the right of the claimant to limit liability; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) if the defendant wishes to –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (i) dispute the jurisdiction of the court; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (ii) argue that the court should not exercise its jurisdiction,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] file within 14 days of service (or where the claim form is served out of the jurisdiction, within the time specified in rule 6.35) an acknowledgment of service as set out in Practice Direction 61. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (8) If a defendant files an acknowledgment of service under paragraph (7)(b) he will be treated as having accepted that the court has jurisdiction to hear the claim unless he applies under Part 11 within 14 days after filing the acknowledgment of service. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (9) Where one or more named defendants admits the right to limit –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) the claimant may apply for a restricted limitation decree in the form set out in Practice Direction 61; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) the court will issue a decree in the form set out in Practice Direction 61 limiting liability only against those named defendants who have admitted the claimant’s right to limit liability. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (10) A restricted limitation decree –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) may be obtained against any named defendant who fails to file a defence within the time specified for doing so; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) need not be advertised, but a copy must be served on the defendants to whom it applies. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (11) Where all the defendants upon whom the claim form has been served admit the claimant’s right to limit liability –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) the claimant may apply to the Admiralty Registrar for a general limitation decree in the form set out in Practice Direction 61; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) the court will issue a limitation decree. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (12) Where one or more of the defendants upon whom the claim form has been served do not admit the claimant’s right to limit, the claimant may apply for a general limitation decree in the form set out in Practice Direction 61. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (13) When a limitation decree is granted the court –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) may –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (i) order that any proceedings relating to any claim arising out of the occurrence be stayed;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (ii) order the claimant to establish a limitation fund if one has not been established or make such other arrangements for payment of claims against which liability is limited; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (iii) if the decree is a restricted limitation decree, distribute the limitation fund; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) will, if the decree is a general limitation decree, give directions as to advertisement of the decree and set a time within which notice of claims against the fund must be filed or an application made to set aside the decree. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (14) When the court grants a general limitation decree the claimant must –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) advertise it in such manner and within such time as the court directs; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) file –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (i) a declaration that the decree has been advertised in accordance with paragraph (a); and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (ii) copies of the advertisements. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (15) No later than the time set in the decree for filing claims, each of the defendants who wishes to assert a claim must file and serve his statement of case on –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) the limiting party; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) all other defendants except where the court orders otherwise. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (16) Any person other than a defendant upon whom the claim form has been served may apply to the court within the time fixed in the decree to have a general limitation decree set aside. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (17) An application under paragraph (16) must be supported by a declaration –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) stating that the applicant has a claim against the claimant arising out of the occurrence; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) setting out grounds for contending that the claimant is not entitled to the decree, either in the amount of limitation or at all. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (18) The claimant may constitute a limitation fund by—

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a )making a payment into court;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) providing security in such form and on such terms as considered adequate by the court; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (c) a combination of (a) and (b),

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] the procedure for which, in each case, is set out in Practice Direction 61

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (19) A limitation fund may be established before or after a limitation claim has been started. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (20) If a limitation claim is not commenced within 75 days after the date the fund was established –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) the fund will lapse;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) all money in court (including interest) will be repaid to the person who made the payment into court; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (c) any security provided will be discharged. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (21) Money paid into court under paragraph (18) will not be paid out, nor will any security provided be discharged, except under an order of the court. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (22) A limitation claim for –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (a) a restricted decree may be brought by counterclaim; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.11] (b) a general decree may only be brought by counterclaim with the permission of the court. ## Stay of proceedings

## 61.12

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.12] Where the court orders a stay of any claim in rem –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.12] (a) any property under arrest in the claim remains under arrest; and

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.12] (b) any security representing the property remains in force,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.12] unless the court orders otherwise. ## Assessors

## 61.13

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.13] The court may sit with assessors when hearing –

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.13] (a) collision claims;

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.13] (b) other claims involving issues of navigation or seamanship; or

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.13] whenever it does so, the parties will not be permitted to call expert witnesses unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.13] (c) a reference as defined in paragraph 13.1 of Practice Direction 61,

[PART 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS > 61.13] (Paragraph 26A of Practice Direction 52C makes provision regarding assessors who assist the Court of Appeal in appeals from decisions of the Admiralty Court.)
